correctness.rationale: The domain of an f^t path requires t successive visited vertices in the domain; a fully selected orbit is never nilpotent. Otherwise the index is one plus the maximum cyclic run of selected vertices. A zero in each allowed word forces a unique closed state itinerary, so the trace counts labeled words, not necklaces. Independent orbit choices give the power n/d, and rotational restrictions are uniquely extended except for the empty map, giving 1−n. At t=1 the trace is one and at t=n every proper subset is allowed. For index t>n/2 only order n is possible; for t<n a unique run of t−1 ones has two distinct delimiters, with n−t−1 free sites, while t=n has one omitted site. For the limit, the probability of order d<s is at most s²/(2n). For d≥s a union bound over n starts gives the upper tail n2^(−s), and at least n/(2s) disjoint length-s blocks give the lower tail exp(−n2^(−s)/(2s)). Taking the two indicated logarithmic scales proves the concentration and vanishing nonnilpotent mass; the rotation/subset sampling bias at the empty map is at most 2^(−n) in total variation, so the conditioning is justified. An independent gap-composition count versus direct walks agrees in every rank/index cell checked for n=2 through 8, including the frozen n=6 and n=8 histograms.
residual_risks: Finite replay does not prove the all-size assertions. Only first-order concentration, not a centered distribution, was verified analytically.

value.rationale: A full rotation rank/index census is well motivated, but that is the already separated component of the prior census. The residual upper-half expression simplifies those same exact layers by marking the unique long run. The additional first-order scale applies ordinary run bounds to a mixture after discarding rare small-order rotations; it gives neither new fluctuation information nor a separate structural conclusion on how rotation arithmetic affects typical indices. These refinements do not establish enough distinct mathematical value for the submitted finding as a whole.
residual_risks: The judgment is on the frozen contribution, not on a future arithmetic or centered distribution theorem.
